title: BMI Calculator
description: Calculate your Body Mass Index (BMI) from height and weight and see your weight category.

formula.summary: BMI compares your weight to your height squared, using metric units, to give a quick screening estimate of whether your weight is in a typical range.

faqs.question: What BMI range is considered healthy?
faqs.answer: For most adults, the World Health Organization defines 18.5-24.9 as 'normal weight', below 18.5 as underweight, 25-29.9 as overweight, and 30+ as obesity.

faqs.question: Is BMI accurate for everyone?
faqs.answer: No - BMI doesn't distinguish muscle from fat, so athletes and very muscular people often show a higher BMI despite low body fat. It's also less reliable for older adults, children, and pregnant people.

faqs.question: Should I use BMI alone to judge my health?
faqs.answer: No - use it as one quick screening signal alongside other measures like waist circumference, body fat percentage, and how you feel, and talk to a doctor about what's healthy for you specifically.

seoContent.heading: What BMI measures and where it came from
seoContent.body: Body Mass Index was developed in the 1830s as a population-level statistical tool, not an individual diagnostic measure, but it remains widely used today because it's simple to calculate and correlates reasonably well with body fat at a population scale. This calculator converts your inputs to metric units automatically and applies the standard formula.

seoContent.heading: Using BMI alongside other health measures
seoContent.body: Because BMI can't tell the difference between muscle and fat mass, it's most useful as a starting point rather than a complete picture. Pairing it with a body fat percentage estimate (like our body fat calculator) and tracking trends over time gives a much more reliable sense of your health than a single BMI number.
